passage:
On the bus ride to school in a Himachal hill town, Yash scrolled past the post: a classmate's torn bag, captioned with a joke, already shared a hundred times. He didn't laugh and he didn't say anything. He just kept scrolling.
All evening the picture came back to him. At home his cousin Aadhya asked, "Why so quiet?" "I saw something and did nothing," he said.
"That's guilt," Aadhya said. "What can you do about it now?"
Next morning Yash reported the post, wrote to the classmate, "Hope you're okay. I'm sorry I said nothing," and didn't forward the picture to anyone. The classmate replied with a small thumbs-up, and the knot in his stomach loosened a little.

qa.q: How many times had the post already been shared?
qa.a: It had already been shared a hundred times.

qa.q: Why did the picture keep coming back to Yash all evening?
qa.a: He felt guilty for having seen the post and done nothing about it. 🤍

qa.q: What did Yash do next that turned guilt into action?
qa.a: He reported the post, wrote a kind message to the classmate and refused to forward the picture.

qa.q: How might the classmate feel on receiving Yash's message?
qa.a: The classmate may feel a bit less alone, as the small thumbs-up suggests, even though the mockery still hurt.

grounding: Shows a teen bystander feeling guilty about a mocking post and reporting it, checking on the target and refusing to share.

passage:
In Nandurbar, the Class 9 group had been passing round a video of Afreen slipping in the rain outside the bus stand, slowed down with silly music. Shankar watched it on Sunday night. Everyone was laughing. He didn't laugh, but he didn't say anything either. He just closed the app.

On Monday, Afreen came to school with her head down and sat alone at lunch. Shankar felt a heavy knot in his stomach. He had seen it. He could have said something.

After lunch, he walked over. "Afreen, I saw the video. I'm sorry I didn't say anything. It was cruel."

She looked up, surprised. "You're the first one to say that."

He reported the video in the group, and when his friend Suresh asked him to forward it, he said, "No. Delete it." Then he told their class teacher, Shinde sir, before the last period. Sir went to the group admin that same afternoon, had the video removed, and spoke to Afreen and her father after school.

qa.q: Where did Afreen slip in the video?
qa.a: Afreen slipped in the rain outside the bus stand.

qa.q: What was Shankar feeling when Afreen sat alone at lunch?
qa.a: Shankar felt guilty, with a heavy knot in his stomach, because he had seen the video and said nothing.

qa.q: What did Shankar do to make up for staying silent?
qa.a: Shankar apologised to Afreen, reported the video, refused to forward it and told Shinde sir the same day.

qa.q: How did Afreen react to Shankar's apology?
qa.a: Afreen was surprised and seemed a little comforted, since he was the first to call the video cruel.

grounding: It shows a teen who saw a mocking post and did nothing, then lets guilt prompt checking on the target, reporting the post and refusing to share it.
